When she complains about workplace harassment, he responds by saying, "Maybe you just need to look at it from a different perspective. Perhaps your boss thinks you're capable. Don't be too anxious; after all, there will always be challenges in work." Crucially, the story explicitly mentions that he says this "to maintain the source of high income." This indicates his motivation is self-serving—he wants her to stay in the high-paying job so he can continue benefiting financially. 

Option A is incorrect because he does not suggest finding a new job; instead, he encourages her to stay. Option B suggests he genuinely believes the boss values her, but the story emphasizes his intent to "maintain the source of high income," implying his motivation is not genuine encouragement but manipulation. Option C focuses on his comment about anxiety, but this is only part of his reasoning—his deeper motive is to keep her in the job for his own benefit. Option D directly reflects this intent: he intentionally suggests the boss values her capabilities to convince her to stay in the high-paying job for his financial gain. 

Thus, the most accurate answer is D.
